title: Shortest path in a binary maze
problemStatement: Given an n×n binary matrix grid where 0 is open and 1 is blocked, return the length of the shortest clear path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1). You may move to any of the 8 adjacent cells. Path length = number of cells visited. If no path exists, return −1.
intuition: Every move costs 1, so BFS on the grid finds the shortest path. Process the queue level-by-level (or store dist in the queue); mark cells visited when enqueued so you do not re-expand them. Eight directions = king moves on a chessboard.

approaches.title: Brute: DFS all paths
approaches.idea: Explore every simple path of 0-cells and take the minimum length. Correct but exponential.

approaches.title: Better: BFS with dist in the queue
approaches.idea: Store (r, c, dist) in the queue. First time you reach a cell is optimal. Same asymptotics as level BFS; slightly more memory per entry.
approaches.whyWorks: Unit cost + BFS ⇒ first visit is shortest.

approaches.title: Optimal: 8-direction BFS (level order)
approaches.idea: BFS from (0,0). Freeze layer size with n = len(queue); bump dist once per layer. Mark grid[r][c]=1 when enqueued. First time you reach the bottom-right, return dist.
algorithm: If start or end is 1 → return -1
While queue: process current layer size; for each cell try 8 neighbors
Enqueue open (0) cells and mark them 1
If queue empties without reaching end → -1
approaches.dryRun: 2×2 [[0,1],[1,0]]: start (0,0) dist=1 → enqueue diagonal (1,1) → next layer returns 2
approaches.whyWorks: Unit step cost + BFS ⇒ first hit on the target is shortest. Marking on enqueue prevents duplicate work.

python.notes: Level-order BFS: n = len(queue) freezes the current layer. Mutates grid as visited (1).

java.notes: Same layer BFS; mark visited when pushing.

cpp.notes: 8-neigh BFS; path length counted per layer.

specialTechnique.title: Grid shortest path
specialTechnique.body:
Clear cells + unit cost → BFS (not Dijkstra).
4-neigh vs 8-neigh only changes the directions array.
Mark visited on enqueue to avoid duplicates.

edgeCases: Fully open grid → diagonal-ish path length n (with 8 dirs)
commonMistakes: Using only 4 directions when the problem allows 8
Incrementing dist per cell instead of per BFS layer (or forgetting to store dist in the queue)
patternRecognition: Shortest path in a binary grid / maze
followUps: Obstacles with weights → Dijkstra on grid?
interviewInsight: Say: “Unit cost on a grid ⇒ multisource/level BFS; 8 dirs for diagonal moves.”
